speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your condition, have you experienced any pain during intercourse, and if so, does it occur before, during, or after penetration? Additionally, have there been any changes in your menstrual cycle or irregularities noted?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the combination of infertility, dyspareunia, and pelvic floor tension is concerning. Given your history of body dysmorphic disorder, have you been experiencing significant psychological distress or anxiety about your body or sexual function recently? REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_Exam.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic Examination - External Genitalia: Normal appearing vulva without redness; Vaginal Examination: No discharge. The initial attempt at speculum examination was aborted due to patient's pelvic floor muscles tensing up and discomfort. Vital Signs - Temperature: 36.8°C (98.2°F); Blood Pressure: 110/70 mmHg; Heart Rate: 75 bpm; Respiratory Rate: 14 breaths/min. Complete Blood Count - WBC: 6,000 /μL; Hemoglobin: 13.8 g/dL; Platelets: 280,000 /μL. Hormonal Profile - FSH: Normal; LH: Normal; Estradiol: Normal; Progesterone: Normal; Testosterone: Normal. Pelvic Ultrasound - Findings: Normal uterus and adnexa with no evidence of fibroids or ovarian cysts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Vaginismus secondary to body dysmorphic disorder. The combination of involuntary pelvic floor muscle spasm preventing speculum insertion, painless (or painful) penetration, normal hormonal workup, and a history of body dysmorphia strongly supports this functional diagnosis rather than organic pathology like endometriosis or infection.
